narrative.overview:
CoreWhore is a dark tool that is always running. The whole system borrows one image: a green prompt blinking on a black screen, waiting for the next job. Surfaces are near-black with a green undertone, text is phosphor-pale, and a single neon green appears only where something is live, selected or actionable. The logo, a neon italic CW_ whose underscore is a blinking cursor, is the origin of every other decision.

The interface is dense and confident rather than decorative. It is an Operate surface: people upload tiles, watch chunks finish, read earnings. Numbers are the content, so they get tabular figures and room. The brand's irreverence lives in the name and the cursor, not in ornament; screens that handle money or identity stay plain and exact.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black green-tinted ground, one neon accent, flat tonal layers instead of shadows.
One sans family for everything; a real-italic monospace used only for the logo.
Live state is signalled by motion that means something: pulsing dot, blinking cursor, filling bar.
Compact controls (40px, 8px radius) and 16px-radius panels; borders do the separating.
Honesty markers: amber "Preview data" and "Simulated" badges wherever numbers are not real.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Neon Cursor covers a small share of any screen. If two unrelated things on one screen are green, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure black, no pure white, no gray. Every neutral carries a green hue.

rules.name: The Amber Means Fake Rule
rules.body: Amber is reserved for unbacked data. Never use it for warnings that are real.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes or is compared uses tabular-nums so columns don't jitter while they tick.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Italic belongs to the logo. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If something must sit above content, separate it with a Rule border and the next tonal step, not a drop shadow.

dos: Do use Neon Cursor only for actions, selection, live state, the chart and positive money.
Do set every changing number in tabular-nums and promote one hero figure per screen.
Do separate with 1px Rule borders and the Void/Panel/Panel Raised steps.
Do show Amber "Preview data" or "Simulated" on anything not backed by the API.
Do keep a 2px Neon Cursor focus outline on every interactive element, and theme selection, caret and scrollbars from the palette.
Do use skeletons shaped like the final content, and make empty and error states say what to do next.
donts: Don't use shadows, glows, glass panels or gradient text.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or use green on inactive things.
Don't nest cards or build pages from same-size icon-heading-text cards.
Don't use italics, or the monospace, outside the logo (monospace remains for addresses and code).
Don't put a small label above a heading or number steps unless the order carries information.
Don't use pure black, pure white or gray; always the green-tinted neutrals.
Don't let motion decorate: the cursor blink, live dot and filling bars carry state; nothing else animates.
